source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: The next 2 boards are much simpler I think. One is ESP32-S3 which is standard and other just connectors for sensorts basically

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text: It is not entirely clear to me which connectors should be on that board

ambiguity.description: The required sensor-board connector inventory is not clear enough for implementation.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
For the sensor board, it has two input connectors coming from the main board — one 4-pin JST-PH 2.0mm for power (5V, GND, 3V3, GND) and one 6-pin JST-GH 1.25mm for signals (SDA0, SCL0, SDA1, SCL1, UART TX, UART RX).
Then it has output connectors going to each sensor module:

\- SCD41 — 4-pin JST-GH (3V3/GND/SDA0/SCL0)
\- BME280 — 4-pin JST-GH
\- ENS160 — 4-pin JST-GH
\- SPS30 — 5-pin JST-ZH 1.5mm (5V, SDA0, SCL0, SEL→GND, GND) — different connector type, matches SPS30 cable
\- ZE08-CH2O — 7-pin JST-GH (matches supplied cable)
\- I2C display — 4-pin JST-GH (3V3/GND/SDA1/SCL1)
\- One spare I2C0 port — 4-pin JST-GH
\- One spare I2C1 port — 4-pin JST-GH

So 10 connectors total. Full pinouts are in the sensor board doc.

routing_warnings.description: This message removes the optional sensor level-shifter provision rather than changing the connector inventory.
The requirement to hardwire the SPS30 SEL input to ground belongs to the independently tracked SPS30 mode-selection behavior.
Moving bottom connectors upward and changing their orientation is a sensor-board mechanical-layout requirement.
In context, the missing sensor-board connectors concern parts availability and manufacturer ordering rather than absence of the required interfaces from the design.
